title.narrative: Health Systems Strengthening through PBF in Borana Zone Phase III

description.narrative: A total of 800,490 people living in the catchment area of the 50 targeted Health Facilities in the 14 project Woredas will benefit from the project implementation.

Ethiopia has made steady improvements towards achieving its main health goals. There is good progress in reducing mortality and morbidity among children and women. Over the last two decades, the under-five mortality rate declined from 166 deaths per 100,000 live births in 2000 to 67 in 2016 and infant mortality rate (IMR) declined from 97 deaths per 100,000 live births in 2000 to 48 deaths per 100,000 live births in 2016. Between 2000 and 2016, the Contraceptive Prevalence Rate increased from 8 percent to 36 percent; births attended by skilled attendants increased from 6 percent to 28 percent and maternal mortality (although still high) declined from 871 maternal deaths per 100 000 live births in 2000 to 412 in 2016. However, Ethiopia remains one of the poorest countries in the world with lagging indicators in maternal and child health, especially neonatal mortality. Equitable access to basic services is a concern, while the quality of services and readiness of facilities to provide quality services is a major hindrance to Universal Health Coverage (UHC). Financial protection from serious illness remains inadequate and is one of the most challenging agendas for the next decades.
In Ethiopia, Cordaid started to showcase PBF in the arid and pastoralist Borana zone. After a participatory design process of six months, the project officially started on May 1st, 2015. Stakeholders involved in the design of the PBF project in Borana were among others the Oromia Regional Health Bureau (ORHB), the Borana Zonal Health Department (ZHD), and 4 Woreda (district) Health Offices. Phase I of the PBF project ended on the 30th of June 2018. Since the results were positive, and contributed to an increase in both the utilization and the quality of health care services, the Borana ZHD and Cordaid jointly designed Phase II: scaling up from 4 to 8 woredas, from 9 to 25 health facilities and from a catchment population of 125,918 to a population of488,556. This phase of the project is a further continuation of the Health System Strengthening in Borena covering all Health Facilities in the Zone. This project is funded by the Embassy of the Netherlands.

Improved availability and accessibility of good quality healthcare at primary and secondary levels in the Borana Zone (Oromia Region, Ethiopia), and a stronger health system at large, which supports the progressive realization of Universal Health Coverage (SDG 3.8) in this geographical area.
